south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park continues to urge visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, rating today's heat risk as Extreme at Phantom Ranch, per the park's key hiking messages page (last updated August 4, 2026). north-kaibab-coconino.note: The North Rim reopened for the 2026 season on May 15 and North Kaibab Trail is open to foot traffic through Phantom Ranch, but the National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and Coconino Overlook due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, falling trees, and flash flooding with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead; the park recommends traveling quickly through that section with limited breaks (key hiking messages page last updated August 4, 2026). A Flash Flood Watch covering Grand Canyon Country, including the North Rim, is in effect from noon to midnight today, August 12, which directly raises the burn-scar flash flood risk in this section. Water sources are offline at the North Kaibab Trailhead and Supai Tunnel; hikers must carry all water needed for that section, though single bottles and gallon jugs can be purchased at the North Rim General Store from 9am to 4pm daily. Grand Canyon National Park rates today's heat risk as Extreme at Phantom Ranch. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet expired August 9, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 12, 2026 morning check. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park (key hiking messages, August 4, 2026); National Weather Service Flagstaff.
